full_judgment:
This application under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, has been filed by the accused-petitioner challenging order No.60 dated 19-6-2019 passed by the learned Divisional Special Judge, Dhaka in Special Case No.22 of 2007 now pending before the learned Divisional Special Judge, Dhaka rejecting the application of the accused-petitioner dated 19-6-2019 with a prayer for supplying 161 statements to the accused-petitioner and for recalling and re-examining PWs 2-5 under section 540 of the Code of Criminal procedure. 

 2. Mr SM Sahajahan with Mr Al-Faishal Shiddique, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the accused-petitioner, submits that the learned trial judge by orders dated 4-1-2017, 7-2-2017 and 11-4-2017 directed the prosecution to submit all the 161 statements before the court for the purpose of supplying the same to the accused-petitioner before commencement of the trial as per requirement of sub-section 7 of section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 but the prosecution did not submit the 161 statements before the court in compliance with the orders of the learned trial judge and, as such, a Rule may be issued and the impugned proceeding may be stayed for ends of justice. 

 4. He then submits that on 19-6-2019, finding no other way, the accused-petitioner submitted an application before the trial judge with a prayer for supplying the 161 statements to him and for recalling and re-examining the prosecution witness Nos.2-5 under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure but the said application was rejected by the learned trial judge though the accused-petitioner is entitled to the 161 statements as per sub-section 7 of section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and on this landscape of the fact, a Rule may be issued and the impugned proceeding may be stayed. 

 7. We have gone through the application along with the prosecution materials annexed therewith and perused the same. We have also heard the learned Advocates for the respective parties at length and considered their submissions to the best of our wit and wisdom. It appears from the record that following the application filed by the accused-petitioner, the learned trial judge by orders dated 4-1-2017, 7-2-2017, and 11-4-2017 directed the prosecution to submit 161 statements before the Court for the purpose of supplying the same to the accused-petitioner before the commencement of trial following the requirement of law as contemplated under sub-section 7 of section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment 1958, but the prosecution did not submit the same to the trial court. Nevertheless the accused-petitioner participated in the trial and cross-examined all the prosecution witnesses. It is noticeable from the record that the evidence of PW 1 was recorded on 30-7-2017 and evidence of PW 7 was recorded on 18-4-2017. As per argument of the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner, the accused-petitioner could not property cross-examine the prosecution witnesses in the absence of 161 statements as he could not take necessary contradictions for want of 161 statements and non-cooperation of the prosecution in not supplying the 161 statements to the accused-petitioner has caused a serious prejudice to him affecting his legal and fundamental right to protection of law sub-section 7 of section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 suggests that the previous statements of witnesses to be examined for the prosecution at the trial shall be supplied to the accused at least one week before the commencement of the trial. Under the circumstances, we are of the view that the accused-petitioner is entitled to have the 161 statements before the commencement of the trial for the purpose of cross-examining the prosecution witnesses and he could not properly cross-examined the prosecution witnesses for want of 161 statements. However, it appears that the FIR was lodged in the year of 1998 and the trial was started in the year of 2017 and in the meantime, the evidence of 7 witnesses has already been recorded by the learned trial judge.
